answer: The public methods that mutate leaves, tags, or connections in memory without ever calling saveData (even with autoSave on) are: `addTags`, `importData`, `importObject`, `importFromJSON`, and `importFromCSV` (which mutates via `processCsvImport`). Every other mutating method does save when autoSave is on, including `addLeaf`, `removeLeaf`, `deleteLeaf`, `tagLeaf`, `updateLeaf`, `connectLeaves`, `connectDirectedLeaves`, and `connectSimilarLeaves` (the latter two via `connectLeaves`). `initializeDefaultData` and `clearAllData` call `saveData` directly, and `loadData` intentionally replaces in-memory data from a file without saving. (Answer taken from the fresh knowledge-tree note "q:unsaved" in repo-C's .rosemary tree, derived from src/Rosemary.js; no repository files were read directly since the note was fresh and directly answered the question.)

7 of the 32 methods declared for Rosemary in index.d.ts are never called by name in any *.test.js file: `updateLeaf`, `getAllTags`, `getLeavesByConnection`, `exportToJSON`, `exportToCSV`, `importFromCSV`, and `getLeafContentAsHTML`. Note: `exportToCSV` and `importFromCSV` are still exercised indirectly, since cli.test.js runs the `export-csv` and `import-csv` commands through the CLI without calling those method names directly.

src/cli.js defines two commands that the CLI section of readme.md does not list: `rosemary` and `hello`. Every command the README lists (add, report, search, connect, related, import-csv, export-csv, delete, clear) is defined in src/cli.js, so there are no README-listed commands missing from the CLI. (One related but separate discrepancy: the README shows `import-csv <file>` and `export-csv <file>` as requiring a path, while the CLI treats that path as optional, defaulting to rosemary-import.csv/rosemary-export.csv.)

The CLI (src/cli.js) resolves the data file in a preAction hook from `-d/--data-file`, then the `ROSEMARY_DATA_FILE` environment variable, defaulting to `rosemary-data.json` in the current working directory, then passes that path to both the constructor and `loadData` (and `report` loads it again). The REST API server (src/api.js) reads only `ROSEMARY_DATA_FILE` at startup and passes it to the constructor and `loadData`; when unset it falls back to the constructor's own default. scripts/visualize.js likewise reads only `ROSEMARY_DATA_FILE`, but when unset computes the default itself via `path.join(process.cwd(), 'rosemary-data.json')` rather than relying on the constructor. Code that constructs `Rosemary` directly sets the path via `options.dataFile` on the constructor. In every case the ultimate default (when nothing is set) is the same: `rosemary-data.json` in the process's current working directory.

Only `connectLeaves` validates anything: for an unknown leaf id it throws "Leaf with id X not found," which the CLI prints in red (still exiting 0) and the REST API returns as a 400 with that message. For the same id given twice, `connectLeaves` just logs a warning ("Cannot connect a leaf to itself.") and returns without connecting, so both the CLI and the API report success. A missing id is handled differently per entry point: commander rejects a `rosemary connect` invocation that lacks two ids before it ever reaches Rosemary, while the API does not validate the request body, so two missing ids are treated as the same id (200, nothing connected) and one missing id triggers the "not found" 400. The relationship type is never validated anywhere in the stack — any string is stored as given, and the default is an empty string.

`npm run release -- patch` runs scripts/release.js, which validates the version argument, requires `git status --porcelain` to be empty, and requires the branch to be main (unless `--force-branch`), stopping there if `--dry-run` was passed. It then runs `npm test --silent`, then `npm version patch -m "chore(release): %s"` (bumps package.json, commits, and tags `v<version>`), then `git push --follow-tags`. Finally it runs `npm publish`, whose `prepublishOnly` script (defined in package.json) reruns `npm test` and then `node scripts/check-release.js`, which checks package.json's name/version, a clean tree, that HEAD carries tag `v<version>` and it's on origin, that the version isn't already on the npm registry, and that CHANGELOG.md mentions the new version — only then does npm actually publish the package.

Three RosemaryLLM methods are missing from the docs/llm.md method table: cosineSimilarity, rebuildMissingEmbeddings, and scoreContextRelevance. The table documents 10 methods (addEnhancedLeaf, generateEmbedding, semanticSearch, resolve, rebuildEmbeddings, buildPromptContext, pruneToTokenLimit, estimateTokens, generateStructuredPrompt, complete), and all 10 of those correspond to real methods on RosemaryLLM — the table does not list any nonexistent method.

buildPromptContext computes relevance for each related leaf as 1/distance + 0.15 per shared tag (max 0.3) + 0.2 if the connecting edge has a type + a recency term (0.1 minus 0.002 per day of age, floored at 0) + 0.2 × cosine similarity when both leaves have embeddings, with the total capped at 1; related leaves come from a breadth-first walk to `depth` (default 2) and are sorted by relevance then distance. Pruning only runs when the estimated token count (JSON length / 4) exceeds `maxTokens` (default 1000), applied in this order: (1) drop related leaves with relevance below 0.5, (2) keep at most 3 remaining related leaves, (3) delete `core.tags`. The result is returned as-is even if it is still over the token budget after these steps.

In src/Rosemary.js, `addTags(tags)`, `renameTag(oldTag, newTag)`, `importData(jsonData)`, `importObject(data)`, `importFromJSON(filename)`, and `importFromCSV(filename, options)` (via its helper `processCsvImport`) all mutate `this.leaves`, `this.tags`, and/or `this.stem` directly but contain no call to `saveData()`, so they never write the data file even with autoSave on. The stored note q:unsaved listed the first five of these but is stale: it predates the newly added `renameTag` method, which removes/re-adds tags on every matching leaf and updates `this.tags` without saving. Every other mutating method (`addLeaf`, `removeLeaf`, `deleteLeaf`, `tagLeaf`, `updateLeaf`, `connectLeaves`, `connectDirectedLeaves`, and `connectSimilarLeaves` via `connectLeaves`) calls `saveData()` when `autoSave` is true; `initializeDefaultData` and `clearAllData` call `saveData()` directly (itself gated on autoSave); `loadData` only loads and is expected not to save.

6 of the 33 methods declared for Rosemary in index.d.ts are never called by name (`.methodName(`) in any *.test.js file: `renameTag`, `getAllTags`, `getLeavesByConnection`, `exportToCSV`, `importFromCSV`, and `getLeafContentAsHTML`. Only Rosemary#connectLeaves validates anything: an unknown leaf id makes it throw `Leaf with id X not found`, the same id given twice just logs a yellow warning ("Cannot connect a leaf to itself.") and returns without connecting, and the relationship type is never checked (any string is stored as-is, defaulting to `''`). The CLI's `connect <id1> <id2>` command requires both ids via commander (a missing id is rejected before connectLeaves runs), then calls connectLeaves in a try/catch — an unknown id prints the thrown message in red and the process exits normally (0), while a self-connect still prints the green "Connected..." success message and saves. The REST API's `POST /api/v1/connect` destructures `id1`, `id2`, `type` from the body with no presence check and calls connectLeaves, returning 400 with the error message for an unknown id; since it adds no validation of its own, two missing ids (`undefined === undefined`) are treated as a self-connect (200, nothing connected) while exactly one missing id produces a "not found" 400. Both the CLI and API pass any given relationship-type string through unchanged.

Running `npm run release -- patch` invokes `scripts/release.js`, which first validates the bump argument, requires a clean tree (`git status --porcelain`), and requires the `main` branch (unless `--force-branch`), stopping early on `--dry-run`. It then runs `npm test --silent`, runs `npm version patch` (which updates `package.json`, commits as `chore(release): %s`, and tags `v<version>`), and runs `git push --follow-tags`. `npm version`'s `postversion`/publish step then runs `npm publish`, which triggers the `prepublishOnly` script in `package.json`: this reruns `npm test` and then `scripts/check-release.js`, which checks that `package.json` has name/version, the tree is clean, prints the current branch, confirms the git tag `v<version>` is at HEAD and exists on `origin`, confirms the version isn't already on the npm registry, and confirms `CHANGELOG.md` mentions the new version before `npm publish` actually uploads the package. (Answer taken from the fresh knowledge-tree note `q:release`, derived from package.json, scripts/release.js, and scripts/check-release.js — no repository files were re-read since the note is current.)

buildPromptContext scores each related leaf's relevance as the sum of: 1/distance; 0.15 per shared tag (capped at 0.3 total); 0.2 if the connecting edge has a type; a recency term of 0.1 minus 0.002 per day of age (floored at 0); and 0.2 × cosine similarity when both leaves have embeddings (overall score capped at 1). Related leaves are gathered via a breadth-first walk to `depth` (default 2) and sorted by relevance, then by distance. Pruning only triggers if the estimated size (JSON length / 4) exceeds `maxTokens` (default 1000), and then proceeds in order: (1) drop related leaves with relevance below 0.5, (2) keep at most 3 of the remaining related leaves, (3) delete `core.tags`. The context is returned as-is even if it is still over budget after these steps.
